meta.note: Activities only. Every hour/admission figure below was copied from the attraction's own site. Where a page did not publish hours, the field is null and flagged.

activities.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art (Fifth Avenue)
activities.hours_note: The Met's Plan Your Visit page publishes tickets, transit, parking and accessibility in full but the hours module did not render for this fetch. Do not print hours you have not read — check metmuseum.org the week of travel.
activities.admission: Adults $30 · Seniors (65+) $22 · Students $17 · Children 12 & under free · NY/NJ/CT students and NY residents pay-what-you-wish
activities.transit: 4/5/6 to 86th St then 3 blocks west (~10 min walk, half a mile); M1–M4 buses along Fifth/Madison to 82nd/83rd
activities.exceptions: Closed Thanksgiving and December 25 (standard Met practice; confirm on the site). Ticket valid for the printed date only.
activities.accessibility: Step-free entrances; mobility scooters allowed; service dogs welcome
activities.rules: Backpacks must be worn on the front or carried; no food/drink except a sealed water bottle; no tripods, selfie sticks or drones; non-flash photography for personal use only; large bags and luggage refused
activities.best_for: Half day minimum — 5,000 years of art; the Temple of Dendur and the European Paintings wing alone are 2–3 hours

activities.name: The Met Cloisters
activities.address: 99 Margaret Corbin Drive, Fort Tryon Park, New York, NY 10040
activities.hours_note: Same page render gap as the Fifth Avenue location.
activities.admission: Same ticket structure as the Met: Adults $30, Seniors $22, Students $17, 12 & under free
activities.transit: A train to 190th St (exit by elevator), then ~10 min walk through Fort Tryon Park, or M4 one stop north. From the Met Fifth Ave the M4 runs direct, ~1 h 25 min.
activities.exceptions: Free public parking in Fort Tryon Park; A-train weekend maintenance is common — check MTA
activities.best_for: Medieval Europe, the Unicorn Tapestries, and the best quiet-in-NYC hour of the trip — but it is a 45–60 min ride from Midtown

activities.name: Museum of Modern Art (MoMA)
activities.admission: Adults $30 · Seniors (65+) $22 · Visitors with disabilities $22 (care partner free) · Students $17 · 16 & under free · Members free. Tickets include all galleries and special exhibitions.
activities.exceptions: Open every day except Thanksgiving and Christmas. Galleries close ~15 min before the Museum. UNIQLO Friday Nights: free for New York State residents 17:30–20:30, ticket must be reserved in advance. Members-only weekend mornings 09:30–10:30 in select galleries.
activities.rules: All bags inspected; backpacks must be checked; no large umbrellas; service animals only
activities.best_for: 2–3 hours; pairs naturally with The Modern (same building) for a lunch-to-dinner day

activities.name: MoMA PS1
activities.admission: Free for everyone (adults, seniors, students, children) — funded by Sonya Yu
activities.transit: 7 / E / M to Court Sq–23 St, or G to 21 St; Long Island City
activities.best_for: Contemporary/experimental shows; only worth the trip if you are already doing Queens (e.g. Meju)

activities.name: Statue of Liberty & Ellis Island (ferry access only)
activities.address: Liberty Island / Ellis Island — ferries from Battery Park (NY) and Liberty State Park (NJ)
activities.admission: National Park entrance is free; the concessioner charges for the ferry, and separately for pedestal/crown access. Ferry price not captured from an official page in this pass — UNVERIFIED, book on cityexperiences.com (the official ferry operator for NPS).
activities.exceptions: Closed Thanksgiving (2026-11-26) and Christmas Day. Access is by ferry only — there is no bridge. Crown access requires a separate reservation made months ahead.
activities.practical: Security screening at Battery Park is the bottleneck; arrive at the first ferry. February wind on the water is brutal — this is the one activity that is genuinely worse in your window than in spring.
activities.best_for: Half day. Grounds-only (no pedestal) is the low-commitment version.

activities.name: Top of the Rock Observation Deck
activities.hours: Daily 08:00–24:00 (live 'OPEN 8 AM – 12 AM' banner on the official ticket page)
activities.admission: Timed admission from $42 · Skip-the-line from $82 · VIP Pass from $185 (guided, priority, Beam + SKYLIFT, champagne toast)
activities.exceptions: Timed-entry slots; sunset slots sell out first. VIP pass gains a Christmas-tree experience 3 Dec–3 Jan only.
activities.best_for: The view that includes the Empire State Building (which the Empire State Building's own deck cannot give you). Go 30 min before sunset.

activities.name: The High Line
activities.address: Elevator/stairs access at Gansevoort St, 14th St, 23rd St, 30th St — Manhattan's West Side
activities.trip_window_hours: Your Feb window falls in the winter schedule — 07:00–20:00 daily.
activities.exceptions: The Rail Yard Preserve section (30th–34th St) closes at dusk. Free docent-led tours run on select days. Elevator outages are posted on a status page — check it if anyone in the party cannot use stairs.
activities.rules: No smoking, bicycles, skateboards or scooters; dogs not permitted (service dogs only); no alcohol outside authorised areas; professional photo/film shoots need a permit
activities.accessibility: Stairs, ramps and elevators at multiple entries; wheelchair loan must be requested at least one business day ahead (requests reviewed Mon–Fri 09:00–17:00). Citi Bike docks and bike racks at street level.
activities.best_for: A 1.5-mile walk; enter at Gansevoort, exit at 23rd, and land in Chelsea for lunch. Cold but empty in February — actually a plus.
